summary: Independent GRAVEYARD expectations/execution pass covered all 12 active-batch companies without contaminating Earth Score. Primary operating evidence shows unusually strong growth across most of the batch, which raises the bar for investment asymmetry: many theses can be operationally correct yet still require aggressive continuation assumptions. Reproducible current-price/consensus/crowding inputs are not available in the canonical pre-T0 record for this cycle, so opportunity precision remains deliberately unknown and no deployment state is proposed. Promotion readiness remains false until company dossiers and valuation/execution inputs are normalized.

perCompanyCoverage.expectationTest: Record $234M quarterly revenue, $2.36B backlog and multiple strategic transactions create a high-expectation path in which Neutron, acquisition integration and backlog conversion must all work. Business progress can be real while execution timing remains poor for capital deployment.
executionRisks: financing/dilution if cash needs exceed plan
unknowns: Current reproducible market cap/enterprise value, consensus expectations, exact transaction financing and near-term cash burn.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: A valuation bridge shows conservative assumptions already discount substantial Neutron/integration failure while liquidity remains ample.

perCompanyCoverage.expectationTest: FY2026 net income and explosive AI-connectivity growth can justify premium expectations, but 32%/33%/19% end-customer concentration means the market may be capitalizing a small number of programs as durable annuities.
unknowns: Current valuation multiple, consensus growth duration and program-level contract visibility.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: Current valuation implies modest growth while customer diversification is demonstrably broadening.

perCompanyCoverage.expectationTest: Q2 revenue of $392.4M with very high gross profit and Scorpio ramp creates strong narrative momentum. Opportunity quality depends on whether valuation assumes many years of platform expansion rather than a small number of concentrated ramps.
unknowns: Current market valuation, exact end-customer mix and forward consensus embedded in price.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: Valuation can be supported by conservative multi-product adoption with no heroic terminal assumptions.

perCompanyCoverage.expectationTest: The operating thesis is exceptionally strong, but investment execution must account for concentrated customers, restricted China access and custom-accelerator substitution. At this scale, maintaining extraordinary growth requires increasingly large absolute AI-capex expansion.
unknowns: Canonical current valuation/crowding/consensus data for this cycle.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: A reproducible valuation bridge shows base-case returns remain attractive under materially slower growth and margin normalization.

perCompanyCoverage.expectationTest: Q2 revenue grew 50% and Data Center represented 58% of revenue. Execution attractiveness depends on how much future Instinct share gain is already required versus what can be earned from EPYC plus incremental accelerator adoption.
unknowns: Current price-implied share-gain assumptions and normalized Instinct gross margin.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: Valuation supports acceptable return with only modest accelerator share gains and no China normalization.

perCompanyCoverage.expectationTest: Q3 revenue grew 86%, AI semiconductor revenue 221%, and Q4 AI guidance is $21.7B. Those figures create an extremely high continuation bar; the right execution question is not whether AI demand is strong but how many years of custom-accelerator hypergrowth the valuation already assumes.
unknowns: Current EV/FCF, AI customer count and consensus duration of 200%+ AI growth.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: Conservative normalized growth/deleveraging assumptions still support attractive return at current valuation.

perCompanyCoverage.expectationTest: Q2 revenue rose 36% YoY, 2nm is already ramping and margins are exceptional. Opportunity must separately price geopolitical tail risk and the cost of geographic replication rather than assuming process leadership automatically equals superior risk-adjusted return.
unknowns: Current valuation and explicit market-implied probability of geopolitical disruption.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: Valuation compensates for substantial geopolitical and overseas-margin penalties while process leadership persists.

perCompanyCoverage.expectationTest: Backlog of €38.8B, 50%+ margins and EUV scarcity support premium quality, but China decline and High-NA adoption timing create a meaningful gap between monopoly-like business quality and entry attractiveness.
unknowns: Current multiple, backlog duration and market-implied High-NA adoption curve.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: Current valuation still offers strong return under slower High-NA adoption and structurally lower China sales.

expectationTest: Asset-light royalty economics can command a premium, but top-five customer concentration, Arm China and SoftBank-linked arrangements mean a clean platform-growth narrative can hide governance and substitution asymmetry.
unknowns: Current valuation, independent data-center royalty mix and consensus terminal royalty assumptions.
falsifier: Attractive return persists under conservative royalty growth and explicit RISC-V/data-center share assumptions.

ready_for_chief.expectationTest: Revenue of $41.46B and gross margins above 80% in key units are far outside historical memory-cycle norms. Execution discipline requires underwriting normalization, not capitalizing current scarcity margins indefinitely.
unknowns: Current through-cycle valuation and contract floors/take-or-pay economics.
ready_for_chief.falsifier: A normalized-cycle valuation remains attractive even if gross margins fall sharply from current record levels.

ready_for_chief.expectationTest: First $3B quarter and near-50% non-GAAP operating margin are elite, but market expectations may already assume Ethernet wins most AI fabric share. Execution requires testing buyer concentration and alternative/custom fabrics before treating growth as uncapped.
unknowns: Current valuation, top-customer share and market-implied AI networking share.
ready_for_chief.falsifier: Valuation supports strong return even if AI networking growth moderates and top customers reduce capex.

ready_for_chief.expectationTest: AI power/cooling scarcity supports demand, but reported backlog can outrun realizable deployment if grid/interconnection, financing or customer project timing slips. Execution must discount backlog until aging/cancellation quality is known.
unknowns: Current valuation, backlog aging and cancellation profile, customer concentration.
ready_for_chief.falsifier: Backlog converts at planned margins with low cancellations and valuation remains attractive after normalizing order growth.

materialFindings.finding: Operating momentum is so strong across much of the batch that expectations risk is now a first-order variable: AVGO guides Q4 AI semiconductor revenue to $21.7B, AMD Data Center is 58% of revenue, MU is reporting record memory margins, and ANET has crossed $3B quarterly revenue.
Current-price, consensus and crowding inputs are not canonical for this pre-T0 cycle; opportunity precision must remain unknown rather than inferred from company quality or recent growth.

MU requires explicit through-cycle normalization because current margins are extreme relative to historical memory economics; RKLB and VRT require backlog-quality normalization before execution confidence can be high.

contradictions: Strong business quality does not imply favorable entry; several batch names are operating at record growth/margin states that can embed demanding expectations.
Backlog and guidance improve visibility but can create false precision when cancellation rights, customer concentration and project timing are not normalized.
unknowns: No canonical, reproducible current-price/market-cap/enterprise-value snapshot exists for all 12 names in this cycle.
Consensus estimates and crowding/positioning are not available from a sufficiently reliable current source for all batch companies.
Opportunity Score, Execution Score and Action State remain intentionally unset pre-T0 rather than fabricated.

peerRequests.request: Provide normalized diluted shares, customer concentration and through-cycle margins needed for reproducible valuation bridges.
Establish a canonical timestamped market-data source before precise Opportunity/Execution scoring is allowed.
Continue stress-testing record-growth assumptions and common AI-capex dependence rather than treating headline growth as independent confirmation.

accuracyDebates.reason: Without canonical current market/consensus inputs, exact valuation or Action State would create false precision and contaminate the quality ranking.
Record operating states at MU, AVGO and other AI-exposed names require normalized scenarios rather than simple extrapolation.
